outcome: Define source-agnostic ContextRequirement and ContextResolution semantics that express runtime context need, budget, provenance, currentness and materialization without leaking provider or application lifecycle authority.
currentProblem: The old semantic boundary was two application-specific pull functions. That shape cannot express runtime semantic retrieval, progressive resolution, explicit context budgets, multiple provider capabilities or durable resolution identity while keeping provider details below Oracle.
constraints: ContextRequirement describes semantic need and limits; it does not contain provider/tool commands or task lifecycle instructions.
ContextResolution binds exact requirement identity, source snapshot/currentness, provenance, materialization identity and consumed budget.
The contract must support current Backend repository and QA accepted-artifact context without hard-coding those as the only provider classes.
Oracle cannot claim, schedule, accept, publish, recover or mutate product truth through the semantic contract.
Required missing, stale or ambiguous context fails closed; partial/optional context must be explicit and bounded.
The contract must be testable deterministically without a live model.
successCriteria: Research defines concrete ContextRequirement and ContextResolution fields, identity rules and lifecycle examples for repository and accepted-artifact use cases.
Budget and progressive-resolution semantics are explicit enough to prevent unbounded retrieval or silent context growth.
Currentness and provenance can be checked deterministically at consumption/replay boundaries.
Negative cases prove the semantic contract cannot confer application/domain authority.
The contract admits semantic-code, lexical-search, graph and artifact providers without exposing provider-specific commands to callers.
